subject: DPA: Medisource - transfer impact addendum and SCCs coordination
messages:
From: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@medisource.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medisource.com
Date: 2025-12-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: DPA: Medisource - transfer annex and SCCs queries

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for taking this on. Attached is the draft DPA and a short list of SCCs concerns raised by our legal team (see transfer-impact-addendum-draft.pdf). Our key asks:
- Confirmation of processor/processor roles for logging and analytics subsystems
- Clarify KMS/keys residency and whether Redwood will persist any customer keys outside EU
- Handling of subprocessor change notices and 30-day review window

We’re on a tight procurement cadence and would like a short call to close open redlines this week. Can you confirm availability?

Attachments: transfer-impact-addendum-draft.pdf

Best,
Sofia Ramos
Senior Contracts Lead
Medisource Health

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@medisource.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, procurement@medisource.com
Date: 2025-12-02T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: DPA: Medisource - transfer annex and SCCs queries

Thanks Sofia — got the draft. Looping in Ben (privacy/inference product) and Laura (legal) for the redline.

Quick summary of what we’ll review today:
1) Roles: we’ll confirm processor/subprocessor mapping for telemetry, embeddings storage, and model serving.
2) Key management: clarify where keys are generated and whether any material is persisted outside EU.
3) Subprocessor change: propose a 30-day notice with an escalation path rather than full consent for every minor subprocessor.
4) SCCs: compare clause variants and propose consolidated text.

I’ve attached our initial annotated redline (DPA_redline_v1.docx) — internal comments are highlighted. Proposal: 30-minute working session Thursday 10 Dec or Friday 11 Dec. Please confirm which works for you.

Attachments: DPA_redline_v1.docx

– Chloe Martin | Senior Contracts Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-12-03T11:14:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: Medisource DPA - quick risk flags

Chloe / Laura / Neha — quick notes from infra POV before legal dive:
- Telemetry: we treat aggregated telemetry as non-identifiable; raw logs that include IP/Timestamp are retained for 30 days by default in EU regions. If client requires shorter retention, we can configure custom retention but it’s an ops ticket.
- KMS: Customer-managed keys (Bring Your Own Key) are supported in our Dedicated/Private offering. For hosted accounts, keys are managed by Redwood; we can restrict key material to EU KMS region, but backup replication (for disaster recovery) may be to an adjacent region (still within EU or APAC depending on customer's preference).
- Subprocessors: Our standard list is here internally — will share a short export for the team. We prefer notice + opt-out window for certain high-risk subprocessors only.

I’ll flag anything that requires an engineering change; otherwise proposals can be handled in contract.

Ben
Ben Carter | Head of Trust & Safety

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@medisource.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-12-04T09:36:00-08:00
Subject: Re: DPA: Medisource - transfer annex and SCCs queries

Sofia / team — attached is a tracked-change version of the SCCs reconciliation and two proposed paragraph options for the transfer-addendum. Key legal proposals:
- Insert explicit processor responsibilities for KV cache and embeddings persistence (Option A: limited retention + audit right; Option B: retention by default with documented operational controls).
- Replace vendor-wide "subprocessor consent" clause with a tiered model:
   * Tier 1 (critical infra): prior written notice + 30-day review
   * Tier 2 (low-risk SaaS): notice-only
- Clarify governing law and remedy carveouts for EU export controls.

See SCCs-comparison.xlsx for a side-by-side of the template SCCs we applied vs Medisource preferred edits. Please confirm which option you prefer and whether your procurement team needs additional assurances (e.g., SOC2 + KMS attestation).

Attachments: SCCs-comparison.xlsx

Regards,
Laura Bennett | Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

From: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@medisource.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medisource.com, James Lee <j.lee@clientcorp.co.uk>
Date: 2025-12-06T14:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: DPA: Medisource - transfer annex and SCCs queries

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A few responses:
- Roles: our product team accepts the Tier 1/Tier 2 split, but wants Tier 1 to explicitly include any subprocessor that stores unredacted customer content.
- KMS: Medisource prefers customer-managed KMS but will accept Redwood-managed EU keys if there is a contractual guarantee (no replication outside EU without prior notice).
- Evidence: procurement confirms SOC2 + a KMS attestation will be sufficient.

I’ve uploaded a revised transfer impact addendum (transfer-impact-addendum-draft.pdf) and started a DocuSign session for the order form (link below) to keep procurement moving while we finalize the DPA language.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/doc/ABC12345
Attachments: transfer-impact-addendum-draft.pdf

Would like to lock language by EOD Monday so procurement can route the order form. Available for call Thu 10 Dec 9:30–10:00 or Fri 11 Dec 14:00–14:30 CET.

Best,
Sofia

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@medisource.com>, procurement@medisource.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-12-08T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: DPA: Medisource - transfer annex and SCCs queries (next steps)

All — thanks for the confirmations. Summary and next steps:

Owners:
- Laura: finalize the SCCs reconciled text (Option A/Option B decision) and provide final tracked version by Mon 2025-12-15.
- Ben: export current subprocessor register and mark any processors that store unredacted customer content by Fri 2025-12-12.
- Neha: confirm KMS technical constraints and whether DR replication can be limited to EU by Mon 2025-12-14.
- Chloe (me): consolidate final DPA redline and send to Sofia for signoff by Tue 2025-12-16.

Proposed short call to finalize open points: Thu 2025-12-10 at 09:30 CET (that maps to 2025-12-10T00:30:00-08:00 for our calendars). Sofia — please confirm and I’ll send calendar invite.

Attachments referenced: DPA_redline_v1.docx; SCCs-comparison.xlsx; transfer-impact-addendum-draft.pdf
Related DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/doc/ABC12345

If anyone sees a blocker to the proposed dates, flag here. Otherwise I’ll schedule the call and circulate an agenda focused on: roles mapping, KMS/replication guarantees, and the Tier 1/Tier 2 subprocessor model.

Thanks — Chloe
